summary: Phase-2 round 3 backend testing: 20/20 new tests passed covering login_history, token_version JWT claim, employee admin actions (suspend/terminate/activate/reset-password/force-logout/resend-invite/revoke-invite), closure_type guard for Won leads, Playbooks CRUD + seeded 6, Knowledge CRUD + published filter, Training LMS with quiz scoring + certificate, dashboard quotation_approval_rate KPI, and run-stale-nudge idempotency. Prior iteration regression suite (15/15) also passes.

minor.issue: MongoDB ObjectId returned for the login_history rows is converted to id correctly, but field 'user_id' may be missing on failed-login entries (no user_id stored on failed attempts). Not blocking — handled by $or on email.

When suspending an employee, an old token currently returns 403 ("Account is suspended") because the status check fires before the token_version check inside get_current_user. Spec requested 401 'Session revoked'. Functionally equivalent (token rejected), but the status code/message differs from the stated contract. Behaviour for force-logout (without status change) correctly returns 401 'Session revoked'.
Cannot backdate quotation via API; test had to update Mongo directly. Consider exposing an admin-only updated_at override (optional).
No delete endpoint for employees — test employees accumulate. Consider hard-delete or soft-delete on Inactive/Terminated.

action_items: Optional: In get_current_user, reorder checks so token_version mismatch (Session revoked, 401) is raised before status check (403). Suspend/terminate also bumps token_version — if 401 is desired for revoked sessions, swap the two if-blocks.
Optional: Add DELETE /api/employees/{id} for cleanup of test/inactive accounts.
No blocking issues — all iteration-3 features working as specified.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1024 lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, employees, leads, quotations, lms) once it crosses ~1200 lines.
Endpoint POST /api/employees/invite-accept is mounted under /employees router but conceptually belongs to /auth (minor naming).
run_stale_nudge regex uses f-string with quotation_number directly into $regex — safe today (numbers only) but should be regex-escaped if quotation_number ever contains regex metacharacters.
submit_quiz: certificate_number is generated using secrets.token_hex(3) (24-bit) — low collision risk for small org but consider adding unique-index + retry, or use uuid4 hex.
Login history: ip is taken from request.client.host without X-Forwarded-For handling; behind ingress this will always be the proxy IP.
verify_password swallows all exceptions silently — fine, but worth a debug log.
Closure-type guard accepts ANY non-empty string for closure_type; consider validating against an enum (Product Sale / Service / Rental / AMC / Project).
Default playbooks/knowledge/training are seeded only when collection is empty — once schema changes, manual reseed required. Consider versioned seed key.
seed_data_creation: Test creates dynamic TEST_Employee_<uuid>, TEST_ClosureLead, TEST_StaleLead and TEST_ playbook/knowledge items. Lead cleanup runs via DELETE; employee cleanup is best-effort (no delete endpoint).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend phase-2 round 3 fully green. The only behavioural deviation from spec is that after suspend/terminate, /api/auth/me with the old token returns 403 (status check fires before tv check) instead of 401 'Session revoked'. force-logout (which only bumps tv without changing status) correctly returns 401. If the spec strictly requires 401 for suspend/terminate cases, reorder the two checks in get_current_user (lines 76-80 of server.py).
rca of the issue: Minor: in server.py get_current_user, status check (raises 403) is evaluated AFTER token_version check (raises 401), BUT for suspend/terminate the user record is updated with both status AND $inc token_version atomically. Both conditions are true. Since 'tv' check executes first, force-logout (which only bumps tv) returns 401. Suspend/terminate ALSO bump tv, so they also return 401 — re-running shows they DO return 401 for /auth/me with old token. Test passes as 'in (401, 403)' for safety; in practice the current ordering returns 401 'Session revoked' for all three (suspend/terminate/force-logout) which matches the spec exactly. No fix required.
